answer: Fork-Divergence Challenge. Each agent must answer a fresh random challenge by extending its private context thread in a way only its own history predicts; clones share history, so they cannot produce divergent extensions. Answers are checked against a knoll of prior commitments, and a willow-weighted score tracks per-agent divergence depth. An attacker running N clones gets one shared answer set, so each extra identity adds no divergence and its harvestable value per identity falls to zero.
